gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: He continued ___ as if nothing had happened.
gaps.explanation: continue takes -ing or to-infinitive. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: Did you remember ___ the window before we left?
gaps.explanation: 'Remember to do' = not forget an obligation; 'remember locking' recalls a past action.

gaps.sentence: It's high time we ___ this attic.
gaps.explanation: it's (high) time + subject + past simple (unreal past): time we cleared.

gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: He spent months ___ the application, only to be rejected in minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time doing something' takes the gerund.
